mainTopic: The שטר מברחת a woman writes to keep property from her husband, and the new משנה on turning a wife's inherited money and produce into land, including the rule for telling produce from principal.
overview: The amud opens with רב נחמן tearing up a gift document a woman had written to her daughter. רב ענן complains to מר עוקבא, who calls it a שטר מברחת and backs רב נחמן with שמואל's ruling that such documents are torn. רבא asks whether a mother might really give to her daughter, and רב נחמן answers that a person still puts herself first. The גמרא then challenges שמואל from a ברייתא implying that an evasion document can work. רבי זירא answers that שמואל's case is when she wrote over all her property, while the ברייתא's case is only part of it. אביי explains that the husband still does not get the property, because it is treated like property he does not know about. A new משנה then teaches that money or produce a wife inherits is used to buy land, and lists three views about produce still growing. The גמרא discusses what to buy, gives a rule for telling produce from principal, and begins a teaching of רבי ינאי about a thief that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב נחמן tears the document
steps.stepSummary: The woman brings her case to רב נחמן, and he rips up the gift document she had written.
steps.simpleTranslation: She came before רב נחמן, and רב נחמן tore up the document.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. The woman who had written her property to her daughter comes to court, and רב נחמן tears up that gift document.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tearing the document means רב נחמן ruled that the gift was never real. The property stays with the mother. The rest of this section asks whether this ruling was justified.

keyTerms.meaning: Before him (coming to him for a ruling)

phrases.english: She came before Rav Nachman,
phrases.notes: "She" is the mother from the earlier part of the story, who had written her property to her daughter.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman tore the document.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story begun before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן voids the mother's gift document by tearing it.

steps.title: רב ענן complains and מר עוקבא asks for the facts
steps.stepSummary: רב ענן protests to מר עוקבא that רב נחמן tears people's documents. מר עוקבא asks what actually happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ענן went to מר עוקבא and said: Look at נחמן the farmer, how he tears up people's documents! מר עוקבא said: Please tell me, what exactly happened?
steps.whatsHappening: רב ענן is upset and complains about רב נחמן. מר עוקבא does not react yet; he first asks for the full facts, which sets up his ruling in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ענן sees the tearing as wrecking a valid document. מר עוקבא wants to hear the facts before judging. The details will decide whether רב נחמן was right.

keyTerms.meaning: Let the master see / look, sir

phrases.aramaic: אֲזַל רַב עָנָן לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּמָר עוּקְבָא,
phrases.english: Rav Anan went before Mar Ukva,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חֲזִי מָר נַחְמָן חַקְלָאָה
phrases.english: He said to him: Let the master see Nachman the farmer,
phrases.notes: Calling him "the farmer" is an insult, like saying he acts without real understanding.

phrases.english: how he tears up people's documents.
He said to him: Tell me, please,
how did the actual incident happen?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲזַל רַב עָנָן לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּמָר עוּקְבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to רב נחמן's tearing of the document.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact facts of the case.

steps.title: מר עוקבא supports tearing a document of evasion
steps.stepSummary: After hearing the facts, מר עוקבא identifies it as a שטר מברחת. He quotes שמואל, who said he would tear up any such document.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ענן said: This and this is what happened. מר עוקבא said: You are talking about a שטר מברחת? This is what רב חנילאי בר אידי said in the name of שמואל: I am one who gives rulings: if a שטר מברחת comes into my hands, I will tear it up.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ענן explains the case. מר עוקבא answers that this kind of document should indeed be torn, and backs רב נחמן with a ruling from שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the case is called a שטר מברחת, the gift is not a real gift. It was written only to keep the property away from the husband. שמואל's ruling shows that tearing such a document is proper halacha, not a careless act.

keyTerms.meaning: Such and such (he told all the details)
A document of evasion: a fake gift meant to keep property away from someone

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic rule of the sugya: a שטר מברחת has no force and may be torn up.

phrases.english: He said to him: Such and such happened.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: שְׁטַר מַבְרַחַת קָא אָמְרַתְּ?
phrases.english: He said to him: You are talking about a document of evasion?

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי אָמַר רַב חֲנִילַאי בַּר אִידִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: So said Rav Chanilai bar Idi in the name of Shmuel:
I am one who issues rulings:

phrases.aramaic: אִם יָבֹא שְׁטַר מַבְרַחַת לְיָדִי — אֶקְרָעֶנּוּ.
phrases.english: If a document of evasion comes into my hand, I will tear it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי אָמַר רַב חֲנִילַאי בַּר אִידִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers מר עוקבא's question and resolves רב ענן's complaint.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The document was a שטר מברחת, and שמואל ruled that such documents are torn.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's statement, passed on by רב חנילאי בר אידי.

steps.title: רבא questions the reason when the gift is to a daughter
steps.stepSummary: רבא suggests רב נחמן's reason is that people do not give up their own interests for others. He then argues that a mother might really give to her own daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רב נחמן: What is the reason? Because a person does not give up his own interests and give to others? That only applies to others, but to her daughter she would give!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks רב נחמן why he treated this gift as fake. He offers a possible reason and then pushes back against it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The assumed reason is that people do not truly give away everything they own to strangers. רבא argues that a daughter is different. A mother could really mean to give to her own child, so the gift might be genuine.

keyTerms.meaning: A person does not abandon his own interests

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַב נַחְמָן: טַעְמָא מַאי?
phrases.english: Rava said to Rav Nachman: What is the reason?

phrases.aramaic: דְּלָא שָׁבֵיק אִינִישׁ נַפְשֵׁיהּ וְיָהֵיב לְאַחֲרִינֵי.
phrases.english: Because a person does not abandon himself and give to others.
That applies to others,
but to her daughter she would give!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַב נַחְמָן: טַעְמָא מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רב נחמן's ruling and tests the reasoning behind it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's treating the gift to the daughter as a שטר מברחת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reasoning that 'people don't give up their own interests' covers strangers, but a mother may truly want to give to her daughter.

steps.title: Even compared to her daughter, she prefers herself
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that even when it is her daughter, a woman puts her own needs first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so: compared with her daughter, she prefers herself.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן defends his ruling. The same reasoning holds even for a daughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא thought a daughter might be an exception. רב נחמן says she is not, because a person's own needs still come first. So the gift was not meant as a real transfer.

keyTerms.meaning: In the place of / when weighed against

steps.whatToRemember: A gift written to keep property away from a husband is a שטר מברחת. Even when the receiver is the woman's own daughter, we assume she did not really mean to give up her property.

phrases.english: Even so:
in place of her daughter, herself is preferable to her.
phrases.notes: He means that when it's her own needs against her daughter's, she puts herself first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extends the original reasoning to cover the daughter too.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A mother truly gives to her daughter, so the gift should stand.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even compared to her daughter, a person prefers herself, so the gift is not real.

steps.title: Challenge begins from רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts a challenge from a ברייתא. It says a woman who wants to keep her property from her husband writes a שטר פסים to others.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: A woman who wants to keep her property away from her husband, what does she do? She writes a שטר פסים to others. These are the words of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge what was just said. This step quotes the source; the actual point of the challenge comes in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא describes how a woman protects her property from a husband: she writes it over to others in a document of evasion. The challenge will build on the חכמים's reply in the next step, which shows that such a document can really transfer the property.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (from a ברייתא or משנה)
That she move away / keep out of reach
A document of agreement (a gift the receivers agree not to actually take)

steps.confusionAlert: This step only quotes the ברייתא. Don't look for the full question here; the challenge itself comes right after.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
One who wants to move her property away from her husband,
how does she do it?
She writes a document of agreement to others,
phrases.notes: The others agree ahead of time not to really take the property; it's just to keep it out of the husband's hands.

phrases.english: the words of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a challenge from a ברייתא against שמואל's ruling, which רב נחמן followed, that a שטר מברחת is void.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling, which רב נחמן followed, that a שטר מברחת is torn up and has no force (steps 1 and 3).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to the חכמים, she keeps her property only because she added the clause 'from today, and when I want.' That implies that without it the recipient acquires, so an evasion document works. Steps 7 and 8 complete this argument.

steps.title: The חכמים say she needs a special clause
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. The חכמים say the recipient can trick her and keep the property, unless she writes 'from today, and when I want.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: if he wants, he can fool her. That stays true until she writes to him: 'from today, and when I want.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the quote of the ברייתא it started in the last step. This sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים worry that the person who received the שטר פסים could really keep the property. Her only protection is a clause saying the gift works 'from today' but only 'when I want.' This detail becomes the basis of the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'laughs at her'; he can fool her and keep the property
'From today, and when I want': a clause that lets her cancel the gift
The Sages, the majority opinion in the ברייתא

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
If he wants, he can fool her.
phrases.notes: 'He' is the person she wrote the property over to. He can hold onto the gift for real.

phrases.english: Until she writes to him
'From today, and when I want.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא quoted in step 6, which the challenge is built on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the חכמים, the recipient can keep the gift unless she writes 'from today, and when I want.'

steps.title: Without the clause, the recipient acquires
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from the ברייתא that without the special clause the recipient really acquires. That suggests a שטר מברחת is valid, against שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason she keeps her property is that she wrote this to him. So if she did not write it, the recipient acquired it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the חכמים and uses it to challenge שמואל and רב נחמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she only keeps her property because of the clause, then a plain evasion document must work. But שמואל said he would tear up such a document. So the ברייתא seems to argue with שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The reason is…'; the opening of an inference from a source
'But if not…'; the flip side of the case
Literally 'buyer'; here, the person who received the property

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא never says outright that the recipient acquires. The גמרא is reading that from what the חכמים leave unsaid.

phrases.english: The reason is that she wrote this to him;
but if she did not write this to him,
the recipient has acquired it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the ברייתא from steps 6 and 7 into a direct challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling, which רב נחמן followed, that a שטר מברחת is torn up and does not work.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חכמים imply that without the clause the recipient acquires, so an evasion document is valid.

steps.title: All her property versus part of it
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא says there is no contradiction. שמואל's case is when she wrote over all her property. The ברייתא is when she wrote over only part.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: it is not difficult. This case is about all of it, and that case is about part of it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא defends שמואל by saying the two sources are talking about different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a woman writes over everything she owns, it is obvious she only meant to hide it from her husband, so the document is void. If she writes over only part, it could be a real gift. That is why the ברייתא needs the special clause to protect her.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is not difficult'; the opening of an answer

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the line for when a שטר מברחת is torn up: when she wrote over all her property.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said: It is not difficult:
This is about all of it,
phrases.notes: 'This' is שמואל's ruling to tear up the document. It applies when she wrote over all her property.

phrases.english: that is about part of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): all of the property versus part of it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא and שמואל seemed to be talking about the same case and to disagree.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל's case is about all her property, so the document is void. The ברייתא is about part of her property, so the gift works unless she adds the clause.

steps.title: Then the husband should acquire it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the recipient does not acquire when she wrote over everything, the husband should get the property as his wife's.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the recipient did not acquire it, let the husband acquire it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions what happens to the property after רבי זירא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the document is void, the property seems to stay hers. A husband normally has rights in his wife's property. So it seems the husband should acquire it, and her plan to keep it from him would fail.

phrases.english: And if the recipient did not acquire them,
let the husband acquire them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from רבי זירא's answer in step 9 and challenges where the property goes.
steps.kashyaTarget: The result of רבי זירא's answer, where the document over all her property is void.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the gift is void, the property is still hers, so her husband should get his normal rights in it.

steps.title: Treated like property the husband doesn't know about
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the חכמים treated this property like property the husband does not know about, following רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: they made it like property the husband does not know about, and this follows רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains why the husband does not get the property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים gave this property the status of property the husband was not aware of. רבי שמעון holds that the husband does not have rights over such property. So the property stays in the woman's own hands.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They made them'; the חכמים gave the property this status
Property the husband does not know about
The תנא from the משנה whose view אביי follows

steps.whatToRemember: A שטר מברחת over all her property is torn up, as שמואל said. The ברייתא's case is only part of her property. Even when the document is void, the husband does not get the property, because it is treated like property he does not know about, as רבי שמעון holds.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
They made them like property that is unknown to the husband,
and this follows Rabbi Shimon.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: עֲשָׂאוּם כִּנְכָסִים שֶׁאֵין יְדוּעִין לַבַּעַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Giving the property a special legal status (property unknown to the husband).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the gift is void, the husband should get his normal rights in the property.
steps.terutzMaskana: The property is treated like property the husband does not know about, so following רבי שמעון the husband does not acquire it.

steps.title: Inherited money or picked produce is used to buy land
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if a married woman inherits money or produce that is already picked, land is bought with it. She owns the land and her husband eats its produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If money came to her by inheritance, land is bought with it, and he eats the produce. If produce that was already detached from the ground came to her, land is bought with it, and he eats the produce.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It says that money or picked produce a wife inherits is not simply spent; it is used to buy land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband is entitled to the פירות (the income) of his wife's property, but the property itself stays hers. Money cannot produce income, so it is turned into land. The wife keeps the land and the husband eats what grows on it. Picked produce is treated just like money.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'fell to her'; came to her by inheritance
Land is to be bought with it
Eats the produce; the husband's right to the income of her property

steps.confusionAlert: 'He eats the produce' does not mean the land becomes his. The land itself stays the wife's. He only gets what it produces.

phrases.english: MISHNA
If money came to her by inheritance,
land is bought with it,
and he eats the produce.
Produce that is detached from the ground:
land is bought with it,
and he eats the produce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic, after the discussion of שטר מברחת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Inherited money and picked produce are used to buy land. The wife owns the land and the husband eats its produce.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: produce still growing is valued and the extra buys land
steps.stepSummary: For produce still attached to inherited land, רבי מאיר says the land is valued with the produce and without it. The difference is used to buy land.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about produce attached to the ground? רבי מאיר says: we estimate how much the land is worth with the produce and how much it is worth without the produce. With the extra, land is bought, and he eats the produce.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks about produce still growing on land she inherited, and רבי מאיר answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר treats the growing crop like money that came to her. It is not the husband's to eat. Its value is measured by the difference the crop makes to the land's price, and that amount is used to buy more land.

keyTerms.meaning: Attached; produce still growing on the ground
The extra; the difference in value

phrases.english: What about produce attached to the ground?
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets, פֵּירוֹת, is the corrected wording. It makes clear we're talking about produce.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
We estimate it,
how much it is worth with the produce
and how much it is worth without the produce,
and with the extra, land is bought,
and he eats the produce.

steps.triggerLanguage: פֵּירוֹת הַמְחוּבָּרִים בַּקַּרְקַע אָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from picked produce to produce still growing, and gives רבי מאיר's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The value the growing produce adds to the land is used to buy land. The husband eats only the produce of that land.

steps.title: The חכמים: attached produce is his, detached produce is hers
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say produce still attached when she inherits belongs to the husband. Produce already detached belongs to her and is used to buy land.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: what is attached to the ground is his, and what is detached from the ground is hers, and land is bought with it, and he eats the produce.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים argue with רבי מאיר about produce that is still growing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the חכמים, growing produce counts as ordinary produce of her property, and the husband is entitled to that. Produce that was already picked when it came to her counts like money. It is hers and is turned into land.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
what is attached to the ground is his,
and what is detached from the ground is hers,
and land is bought with it,
and he eats the produce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי מאיר about attached produce.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Attached produce goes to the husband. Detached produce is the wife's and is used to buy land.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: a gain at the start means a loss at the end
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון gives a balancing rule. Where the husband gains when she enters the marriage, he loses when she leaves it, and the reverse.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: where his power is strong when she comes in, his power is weak when she goes out. Where his power is weak when she comes in, his power is strong when she goes out.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון states a general rule. In the next line he explains it with an example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Coming in' means the start of the marriage, and 'going out' means a divorce. רבי שמעון says the husband's rights balance out: the kind of produce that favors him at one end favors her at the other.

keyTerms.meaning: His power is strong; he has the stronger claim
His power is weak; he has the weaker claim
Her coming in; the start of the marriage

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
Where his power is strong when she comes in,
phrases.notes: 'His' means the husband's. 'Comes in' means when she enters the marriage.

phrases.english: his power is weak when she goes out.
Where his power is weak when she comes in,
his power is strong when she goes out.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר מְקוֹם שֶׁיִּפָּה כֹּחוֹ בִּכְנִיסָתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third view built on balancing the start and the end of the marriage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The husband's advantage at one end of the marriage is matched by a disadvantage at the other end.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's example: attached and detached produce
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון applies his rule. Attached produce is his at the start and hers at divorce. Detached produce is hers at the start and his at divorce.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? Produce attached to the ground: when she comes in it is his, and when she goes out it is hers. And what is detached from the ground: when she comes in it is hers, and when she goes out it is his.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון explains his general rule with the example of attached and detached produce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the wedding, crops still growing on her land go to him, like the חכמים say. But if he divorces her, crops still growing then stay with her land. Picked produce she brings in is hers. Produce that was already picked during the marriage, when he divorces her, is his.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? It introduces an example.

steps.whatToRemember: There are three views on growing produce. רבי מאיר: its value buys land for her. חכמים: attached is his, detached is hers. רבי שמעון: it flips between the start of the marriage and divorce.

phrases.english: How so?
Produce attached to the ground:
when she comes in, it is his,
and when she goes out, it is hers.
And what is detached from the ground:
when she comes in, it is hers,
and when she goes out, it is his.
phrases.notes: At divorce, produce that was picked during the marriage is his, because the produce of her property was his all along.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the concrete example of רבי שמעון's general rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Attached produce is his at the start of the marriage and hers at divorce. Detached produce is hers at the start and his at divorce.

steps.title: Obvious cases: which purchase wins when the couple disagree
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says it is obvious which purchase is preferred when one spouse wants to buy one kind of property and the other wants another. The longer-lasting choice wins.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: It is obvious: land or houses — land. Houses or date palms — houses. Date palms or other trees — date palms. Trees or grapevines — trees.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by listing cases it calls obvious. This sets up the next, harder question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said land should be bought. In practice the spouses may disagree about what to buy. He wants more produce now; she wants the property to last. The rule is to buy whatever lasts longer, so the wife's property stays safe.
steps.confusionAlert: When the גמרא says 'פשיטא' like this, it is usually clearing away the easy cases so it can ask about a harder one next.

phrases.english: GEMARA: It is obvious:
Land or houses — land.
phrases.notes: One spouse wants one purchase and the other wants the second. The first one named wins, because it lasts longer.

phrases.english: Houses or date palms — houses.
Date palms or trees — date palms.
Trees or grapevines — trees.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה's rule that land is bought, starting with the simple cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the spouses disagree, the more lasting purchase is preferred: land over houses, houses over palms, palms over other trees, trees over vines.

steps.title: Hawthorn forest and fishpond: produce or principal?
steps.stepSummary: There is a dispute whether a hawthorn forest or a fishpond the wife inherits counts as פירא or קרנא.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she inherits a forest of hawthorn trees, or a fishpond, some say these count as produce and some say they count as principal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two unclear kinds of inherited property and reports two opinions on whether they count as produce or as principal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If something is פירא, the husband may use it, since he has rights to the produce of her property. If it is קרנא, it must be kept as her principal. A hawthorn forest and a fishpond are hard to place, so the opinions split.

keyTerms.meaning: Hawthorn trees, which give low-quality fruit
Produce, which the husband may use
Principal, the base property that must be preserved

steps.confusionAlert: פִּירָא דְכַוְורֵי (a fishpond) and פֵּירָא (produce) look almost the same, but they are different words.

phrases.english: A forest of hawthorn trees,
and a fishpond,
some say it is produce
and some say it is principal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי לַהּ פֵּירָא וְאָמְרִי לַהּ קַרְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion of the wife's inherited property by bringing borderline cases of produce versus principal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a dispute whether a hawthorn forest or a fishpond counts as produce or as principal.

steps.title: The rule: does the trunk grow back?
steps.stepSummary: Anything whose trunk grows back after cutting is פירא. Anything whose trunk does not grow back is קרנא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The general rule is this: if the trunk grows back, it is produce. If the trunk does not grow back, it is principal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives one simple test for deciding all such cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test is whether the thing renews itself. If you can cut it and it grows back, taking it does not shrink the base property, so it is produce. If cutting it uses up the property for good, it is principal.

keyTerms.meaning: The general rule of the matter

steps.whatToRemember: Grows back = פירא, which the husband may use. Does not grow back = קרנא, which must be kept as her property.

phrases.english: The general rule of the matter:
if its trunk grows back, it is produce;
if its trunk does not grow back, it is principal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a general rule that settles the kind of question raised in the dispute.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether the trunk grows back decides whether something is produce or principal.

steps.title: New teaching from רבי ינאי about a thief
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a new teaching from רבי ינאי, passed down in two versions of who said it, about someone who steals.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said in the name of רבי אושעיא in the name of רבי ינאי (and some say רבי אבא said it in the name of רבי אושעיא in the name of רבי ינאי): One who steals...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new teaching. It gives the chain of names and only the opening words, 'one who steals.' The rest comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two versions of the chain differ only in the first name, רבי זירא or רבי אבא. Both trace the teaching back to רבי ינאי through רבי אושעיא. The content of the ruling has not appeared yet.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (another version of who said it)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said that Rabbi Oshaya said
that Rabbi Yannai said,
and some say Rabbi Abba said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי:
phrases.english: that Rabbi Oshaya said that Rabbi Yannai said:
One who steals

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching after the produce-versus-principal rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the opening of the teaching, about one who steals, appears so far. The ruling continues afterward.
